what: The bridge from RawrXDGgufReader to a Deep2 execution plan. For any GGUF it classifies the plan family, emits the per-block kind schedule, counts distinct block signatures to detect hybrids, and verifies every tensor is sized by the canonical QuantTypeTable. It does not execute anything.
classification_rule: SSM+MoE when SSM and MoE tensors are both present, SSM when only SSM, expert-MoE when MoE tensors are present, dense-transformer when attention and MLP are present and none of the above. The rule reads tensor names, not a model-name lookup table.

decisive_finding_for_deepseek2.detail: Block 0 carries a dense FFN (ffn_down.weight, ffn_gate.weight, ffn_up.weight). Blocks 1 to 26 carry MoE instead: ffn_gate_exps, ffn_up_exps, ffn_down_exps, ffn_gate_inp, plus the shared-expert tensors ffn_gate_shexp, ffn_up_shexp and ffn_down_shexp.
decisive_finding_for_deepseek2.why_it_matters: Any execution plan for this model must emit a dense FFN block for layer 0 and an MoE block for layers 1 to 26. A single repeated block template is not sufficient, and this is the first thing to get right when generating its ExecutionIR table. The existing pre-generated table is for DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat only and cannot be reused.

why_the_pre_generated_table_blocks_p0_3: The executor dispatches GEN::kExecutionIRTable, a pre-generated 300-operation table bound to DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat tensor names, arena ids and shapes. There is no general generator in the tree. Running deepseek-coder-v2-16b therefore requires generating a new table, and this bridge is what makes that generator verifiable: it states the block kind schedule and the required role inventory before any table is emitted.
other_plan_findings: nemotron_h_moe has 4 distinct block signatures, not the 2 that "SSM blocks alternate with attention blocks" would suggest. Blocks also differ in whether they carry MoE.
deepseek4 has 4 signatures as well, and carries indexer tensors that deepseek2 does not have, so the two must not share a plan.
qwen35, qwen3next, ornith-1.5 and qwen3.8 are hybrids too, confirming the SSM+MoE work is shared across several architectures rather than Nemotron-specific.
39 of 56 files are dense-transformer with a single uniform block signature, which is the cheapest family to support and the natural next target after deepseek2.
what_this_does_not_establish: No model is executed. No logits, tokens, TPS or parity result for any of the 56 models.
A plan family classification is not an execution plan. Building a family plan still means writing the block op sequence, transferring arena ids and binding tensor names.
Discoverable and plannable are still not executable. Deep2 can run only deepseek2.
next: Generate an ExecutionIR table for library__deepseek-coder-v2__16b.gguf using this bridge: dense FFN at block 0, MoE at blocks 1 to 26, MLA attention throughout.
Run prefill and multi-token decode against it, then validate against an independent reference.
Then extend by family, starting with the 39 dense-transformer models.
